BACONC RepubJjc of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.diiq.qov.pn s. 2024. OPINION NO. BC TY bcty2023@gmaiI.com Sir/Madame: This refers to your earlier electronic mail wherein you are seeking for this Department's legal opinion regarding Foreshore Lease Agreement. According to your e-mail, one of the requirements for getting a Foreshore Lease Agreement was the was the Certification of No Conflict or Objection from the Barangay. However, you stated that the Punong Barangay cannot release such certification because said area applied for by the particular littoral owner are being occupied illegal settlers, and you alleged that due to political and personal interests, the Punong Barangay does not want to issue the certification as it might affect him in the upcoming barangay election. Moreover, you claim that the illegal settlers residing in the said foreshore area have applied and have already availed the housing units from the National Housing Authority (NHA) and have been reprimanded by the government to leave the "No Dwelling Zone" area after Super Typhoon Yolanda or Haiyan. In addition, per the NHA, one of the requirements before availing the said unit, was to destroy their previous houses at the "No Dwelling Zone" but this policy was not followed by the past administration of a particular town. Under this premise arose the request for legal opinion regarding the following matters: 1. Is there any other recourse or remedy if the barangay captain does not want to release such Certification? Can an applicant not submit such Certification? Is the Certification a "significant" requirement in applying for Foreshore Lease Contract? 2. A particular riparian or littoral owner got a Provisional Permit (for Foreshore Lease) from CENRO. Can this permit be used to utilize the said foreshore area applied for even if it is not yet the Foreshore Lease Contract of 25 years? At the outset, while it is true that local government units have jurisdiction over territories within their locality, please be informed that in order not to preempt the action/s of other concerned agencies, we deem it proper not to act on the queries that are cognizable by said agencies. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Considering that the issue appears to fall under the mandate and technical expertise of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), we deem it proper to defer to said agency's position. Be that as it may, for your guidance, we deem it proper to cite certain rules which we find applicable to the issue you have raised. Under Section 8 of DENR Administrative Order No. 2004-24 dated August 24, 2004 or the Revised Rules and Regulations Governing the Administration and Management of Forsehore Lands, Foreshore Lease Application or renewal thereof shall be filed with the Community Environment and Natural Resources Office (CENRO) which has jurisdiction over the area. A Certificate of No Objection from the Barangay does not appear to be among those required as necessary or supporting documents in an application for a Foreshore Lease. Correspondingly, in view of the passage of Republic Act No. 11032, otherwise known as the "Ease of Doing Business and Efficient Government Service Delivery Act of 2018", the Certificate of No Objection from the Barangay is no longer necessary considering that a Foreshore Lease Agreement is an agreement executed by and between the DENR and the applicant to occupy, develop, utilize, and manage the foreshore lands, which may also cover marshy lands or lands covered with water bordering upon the shores or banks of navigable lakes or rivers. Note, however, that as to the provisional permit, we deem it proper to emphasize that it is different from a Foreshore Lease Agreement. In this regard, it would be more prudent for you to clarify further with the DENR regarding its scope and limitations. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY THE AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY. JUAN VICTOR R.
